registered: 2026-10-15, before any set 4 candidate was collected or read. Code under test frozen at the commit that adds this file (journey and lessons unchanged since a0a0eb1).
question: On genuinely new real buying questions, does category teaching (D = generic repairs + ADOPTED_LESSONS250) improve decision quality over the generic repairs alone (R) and over Phase249 (A)?

arms.A: Phase249 journey round 3: worktree at e8c9d36, scripts/phase248-journey-eval.mjs, CATEGORY_REGISTRY248

stores: Every arm runs on its own copy of the same base snapshot: pee-knowledge commit f9f20cc (Phase249 products, 2,385 declarations; no Phase250 lessons). D applies its lessons to its copy. Products and declarations are therefore identical across arms.

collection.source: Stack Exchange API only (api.stackexchange.com, via the container proxy); site pages are never fetched (robots.txt Disallow: /). Evaluation use, CC BY-SA attribution per case.
collection.queries: per site, search/advanced sort=relevance pagesize=50 for each of: 'buy', 'recommend', 'which should I', 'looking for', 'worth'
collection.excluded_ids: every question id in Phase248-250 benchmarks and in the Phase250 candidate pools (already seen by the author)
collection.order: eligible candidates of a site are ordered by sha256('<site>:<question_id>') ascending; the first ones passing screening fill the quota
collection.screening: a candidate is excluded only for: no licence field; not a question about choosing, buying or replacing a product (e.g. recipe, technique, repair of an owned item, where-to-buy a consumable); non-English; duplicate of an included question. Every exclusion is recorded with its reason. Inclusion is never decided by whether a curriculum covers the product.

gold.labels: evaluation/phase250/need-catalogue.json (unchanged). expectedCategory: catalogue id | other:<name> | null (no purchase decision) | ambiguous (several products, none chosen). expectedConcepts: catalogue needs of that category. unlistedNeeds: other needs (catalogue categories only). expectedBudget when the user states an anchored limit with an explicit currency. expectedBehaviour: advise | out_of_scope | clarify. candidates: for clarify, the categories in play. tags: accessory, rejected_product, owned_product, multiple_products, implicit_need, negation, physical_constraint, long_request.
gold.author: Claude, from the excerpt text only, before any arm runs. T2: not author-independent, not adjudicated.

decision_quality.advise: correct if the arm's category equals the gold category; harmful if it chooses another definite category; unhelpful abstention if null or ambiguous
decision_quality.out_of_scope: correct if the arm chooses no category (null); unhelpful if ambiguous; harmful if it chooses a definite category
decision_quality.clarify: correct if ambiguous or no category with a clarify decision; premature if it chooses one of the gold candidates; harmful if it chooses a category outside them

scoring.needs: tp/fp/missed per catalogue need id over all cases; recall over listed needs and over listed+unlisted; precision; false needs on out_of_scope cases reported separately
scoring.budget: an expected budget must be found exactly (currency and max); a budget found where none is expected is an error
scoring.paired: per case, D vs R and R vs A: wins, losses and ties on decision quality (correct > unhelpful > premature > harmful) and on needs (tp minus fp)
scoring.primary: decision quality (correct and harmful counts) and need precision/recall; no significance claims at this sample size

after_first_run: set 4 is spent for tuning; subsequent changes are reported as development
